expectation: Membrane ring on scattered small lymphocytes, mostly CD8+ T cells, sitting among the epithelial cells and in the lamina propria of the mucosa, plus a few dendritic cells. Moderately common in the mucosa, rare in the muscle wall, absent off the tissue.
observed: A: haze over the whole tissue, the slide background is lit, and the muscle stripes and mucosal edge glow. B: fibrous haze. C: diffuse rim around a lumen with a few bright specks. D: blurry blob, no ring. E: CD103 is texture, with green strands on CD8a-negative tissue.
why: The signal follows the tissue outline, the autofluorescent muscle and the slide background, and does not pick out CD8a-positive cells or show membrane rings on lymphocytes.
notes: CD103 shows as haze across the tissue and slide, brightest in the muscle stripes and along the edges. Specks around a lumen in C are not clear ring-shaped cells, and in row E the signal lies off the CD8a cells as much as on them.
